verdicts.reason: Both score narration of prior involvement in the same docket with identical exemplars (prior filings, amendments, pilots, waivers, precedents) and the same 0 anchor; Y is only a compressed restatement.
Both require the commenter's own numeric/monetary compliance-cost estimate with its basis or source stated, so the same submissions would top and bottom out on each.
Both reward a concretely specified alternative regulatory design implementable as written and give 0 for mere objection with no proposal.
Identical property (a stand-alone emotionally loaded hook line preceding substantive content) with the same 10 and 0 anchors; Y only adds an interpolating 5 anchor.
Both place reasoning/evidence-driven persuasion at 10 and capitalization, repetition, insults, or hyperbole substituting for argument at 0; Y only spells out the midpoint.
Both score the same surface list of ingest/production artifacts (OCR corruption, duplicated headers, email routing, attachment placeholders, odd spacing, extraction errors) against clean prose.
Both ask whether a practicable alternative design advancing the stated objective while curing the identified defect is offered, with the same 0 anchor of withdraw-or-enforce.
Both require pairing a specific plausible secondary harm with a concrete safeguard, monitoring step, exception, or contingency, and 0 for pathway-free harm prediction.
Both score firsthand observation aimed at a named factual premise the agency relies on, with the same three anchors and the same illustrative assumption types.

Both test whether the instrument would bind at all using the same four probes (limit above practice, threshold never triggered, voluntary approach already failed, model resolution) and the same 5 and 0 anchors.

X measures a developed argument that the statute does not authorize the rule while Y measures the mere presence of part/section CFR citations; a heavily cited comment can make no authority argument and vice versa.
Both score praise of the agency, its staff, effort, priorities, or process, excluding the pro-forma thanks and third-party praise of the policy goal, with matching 10/5/0 anchors.
X scores emotional intensity of expressed feeling while Y scores whether the commenter describes their own operational practice; a flat, detailed practitioner comment scores 0 on X and 10 on Y.
Both score verbatim repetition of a sentence or phrase as a surface property with the same three-or-more-times 10 anchor and no-repetition 0 anchor.

Both score adversarial legal-brief posture from the same feature list (statutory conflict claims, plain-text mandates, legal jeopardy or violations, requested remedies); Y only adds a 5 anchor and a correctness caveat.
Both ask whether mandatory and discretionary elements are separated and reasoned about, with the same undifferentiated-treatment 0 anchor; Y merely adds a passing-mention midpoint.

Both require identifiable, checkable support (studies, datasets, statutes, official analyses, described observations) with relevance and limitations explained, and 0 for vague 'studies show' references.
Both score engagement with costs, competing interests, or reasons for the opposite position, with the same weighing-a-genuine-tradeoff 10 and one-sided-unawareness 0.
Both require concrete explanation of how parties would implement, administer, document, or comply plus named operational obstacles, scoring abstract treatment at 0.
Both score whether intermediate causal steps make the claimed effect checkable, with the same A-B-C illustration, one-link 5, bare-assertion 0, and the same do-not-judge-the-conclusion caveat.
Both score whether a requested change is anchored to an identified paragraph, section, or table, with the same 0 anchor; Y only adds a broad-part midpoint and restates the merit caveat.
Both score density of the same formal filing conventions (address block, Re:/docket caption, membership footnotes, formal salutation, titled signature) against plain conversational text.
Both require targeting a specific premise, dataset, model, or inference with evidence or reasoning that could revise it, scoring mere disagreement with the conclusion at 0.
Both score only the presence of a stated count of members, employees, customers, or constituents, with the identical never-judge-strength caveat.
Both score foregrounded organizational-scale claims from the same list (membership, customers, assets, market share, national reach, prestige) against no such claim.
Both score inside-the-operation granularity across the same categories (workflow, equipment, filing, validation, staffing, transition, compliance process) with the broad-policy-preferences 0 anchor.
Both require locating a particular gap in the agency's notice, preamble, or impact analysis and explaining its bearing, with the same unlocated-allegation 5 and record-never-engaged 0.
Both score specificity of the requested fix on the same scale from exact replacement wording, numeric threshold, or unambiguous procedural change down to a bare for/against position.
Both score whether a conflict with quoted or precisely cited controlling text is demonstrated rather than asserted, with matching 10, 5, and decorative-citation 0 anchors.
